source_meta._title: Loading a custom structure doesn't load rails correctly

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition in the first listed affected version, Minecraft 1.10. Use a fresh single-player world as a deterministic practical choice, with Creative mode and cheats enabled. A flat, unobstructed building area is recommended but is not a report requirement. The original Step1.png attachment must be available because the report makes the rail pattern and its cardinal orientation dependent on that screenshot.
preconditions: Install and select the unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 1.10 profile; do not use the fixed version 25w16a.

Make the report attachment Step1.png available to the executor. It is required to reconstruct the source rail art and its world-relative orientation. Step2.png depicts post-trigger material and must not be used as the source layout.
Use Creative mode, as specified by the report.
Enable cheats so that the unobtainable-from-normal-inventory structure block can be acquired with a command.
Use a fresh world or a structure name that has not already been loaded in the current test world, so the eventual placement is the first actual load of this saved structure.

Do not apply a mirror or rotation during the primary reproduction. A later report comment documents rotation-related variants, but the original procedure and another confirmation state that the problem can occur with no rotation.
Do not continue if Step1.png cannot be retrieved or its cardinal orientation cannot be determined; substituting invented rail geometry would not faithfully reproduce the report.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the exact Java Edition profile named Minecraft 1.10 and start the game without mods.
steps.success_cue: The main menu displays Minecraft 1.10 as the running version.

steps.action: Create a new single-player world. Set Game Mode to Creative and ensure cheats are allowed. A Superflat world may be selected to provide an unobstructed test area, but Superflat is only a practical execution choice.
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative; Allow Cheats: ON
steps.success_cue: The world-generation process begins with Creative mode and commands enabled.

steps.action: Wait for the player to enter the world. Do not begin building until nearby terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player can move and look around normally, and the nearby terrain is fully visible.

steps.action: Press F3 to display the debug overlay. Use its facing direction and X/Y/Z coordinates to select an unobstructed building location and to preserve the exact north/south/east/west orientation shown in Step1.png. Record the lowest and highest coordinates that will contain the copied structure as Xmin, Ymin, Zmin and Xmax, Ymax, Zmax.
steps.success_cue: The debug overlay is visible, the cardinal directions can be determined, and an unobstructed source location has been selected.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat.
steps.success_cue: The chat command-entry field is open.

steps.action: Enter the structure-block acquisition command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter. The quantity of 2 supplies one block for saving and one for loading.
steps.success_cue: Two structure block items are added to the player's inventory or hotbar, and no command-syntax error is shown.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory with E. Obtain ordinary rails and every solid support block needed to reproduce Step1.png. Move the rails, support blocks, and structure blocks into hotbar slots; the hotbar is the row of nine immediately selectable slots at the bottom of the inventory.
steps.success_cue: Rails, all required support blocks, and two structure blocks are available in the hotbar or inventory.

steps.action: Study Step1.png before placing blocks. Identify every support-block and rail position, including any elevation changes, curves, adjacent tracks, and straight sections. Relate the screenshot's indicated world directions to the cardinal directions shown by F3. Do not rotate or mirror the pattern for convenience.
steps.success_cue: Each block position and the required north/south/east/west orientation of the source build have been mapped to the chosen location.

steps.action: Close the inventory with E or Esc. Select the required support block from the hotbar and place the complete support foundation shown in Step1.png. Use right-click to place each block. Keep the entire build within the structure-block size limits exposed by Minecraft 1.10.
steps.success_cue: A complete solid foundation matching Step1.png is present, with an exposed upper surface at every location where a rail must be placed.

steps.action: Select the ordinary rail item in the hotbar. Place rails with right-click on the prepared support blocks until the layout matches Step1.png exactly. Preserve the screenshot's world-relative orientation; in particular, do not interchange north-south and east-west sections.
steps.success_cue: From above, the source rail layout, its curves or neighboring lines, and its cardinal orientation match Step1.png.

steps.action: Stop placing or removing blocks and allow all rail neighbor updates to finish. Walk or fly around the source once and verify that every rail remains supported and that the source has reached a stable shape before saving it.
steps.success_cue: No rails are dropping as items or continuing to change shape, and the intact source still matches Step1.png.

steps.action: Using the F3 coordinates, determine the inclusive bounding box containing all blocks that must be saved: Xmin through Xmax, Ymin through Ymax, and Zmin through Zmax. Include the supporting blocks as well as the rails. Do not include either structure block in this bounding box.
steps.exact_input: Size X = Xmax-Xmin+1; Size Y = Ymax-Ymin+1; Size Z = Zmax-Zmin+1
steps.success_cue: The minimum and maximum coordinates and all three positive structure dimensions have been recorded.

steps.action: Select a structure block in the hotbar and place it one block west and one block north of the bounding box's minimum corner, at the same Y level as Ymin. In coordinate form, place it at Xmin-1, Ymin, Zmin-1.
steps.exact_input: Save structure block position: (Xmin-1, Ymin, Zmin-1)
steps.success_cue: A structure block is adjacent to but outside the source structure's bounding box.

steps.action: Right-click the placed structure block to open its interface. Click the mode button in the lower-left until the interface is in SAVE mode. In Minecraft 1.10 this button may initially display DATA.
steps.success_cue: The structure-block interface visibly indicates SAVE mode and exposes structure name, relative position, and size fields.

steps.action: Enter a unique structure name in the structure-name field. Use the same spelling and capitalization during loading.
steps.success_cue: The structure-name field contains rail_art_mc104231.

steps.action: Set the save block's relative-position fields so the saved region begins one block east and one block south of the structure block, at the same height.
steps.success_cue: The save interface shows relative position 1, 0, 1.

steps.action: Enter the inclusive bounding-box dimensions calculated in step 12 into the structure-size X, Y, and Z fields. If the interface provides a bounding-box display option, enable it and confirm visually that the outline contains every support block and rail but excludes the structure block.
steps.success_cue: The displayed or calculated save volume encloses the complete rail build and its supports, without enclosing the save structure block.

steps.action: Leave entity inclusion disabled unless Step1.png unexpectedly contains an entity that is explicitly part of the rail art. Click the SAVE button on the right side of the interface once.
steps.exact_input: Structure name: rail_art_mc104231; Include Entities: OFF; press SAVE
steps.success_cue: Minecraft reports that rail_art_mc104231 was saved, and the source build remains intact.

steps.action: Move to another unobstructed location far enough away that a copy of the entire saved bounding box cannot overlap the source build or its structure block. Wait until the destination chunks have rendered. Designate the intended minimum corner of the loaded structure as TX, TY, TZ, with enough empty space above it for the full saved height.
steps.success_cue: The destination chunks are rendered, movement is responsive, and the complete saved structure can fit without overlapping the source.

steps.action: Select the second structure block and place it one block west and one block north of the destination minimum corner, at TX-1, TY, TZ-1.
steps.exact_input: Load structure block position: (TX-1, TY, TZ-1)
steps.success_cue: A second structure block is present next to the empty destination volume.

steps.action: Right-click the destination structure block. Click its lower-left mode button until the interface is in LOAD mode.
steps.success_cue: The structure-block interface visibly indicates LOAD mode.

steps.action: Enter the exact saved structure name and set the relative load position to one block east and one block south of the load structure block, at the same Y level. Keep mirroring disabled and select the unrotated 0-degree setting.
steps.exact_input: Name: rail_art_mc104231; Relative Position: X=1, Y=0, Z=1; Mirror: NONE; Rotation: 0 degrees
steps.success_cue: The LOAD interface contains the matching name and position, with no mirror and no rotation selected.

steps.action: Click LOAD once to prepare or locate the saved structure. This preparatory click is not the first actual structure placement. Do not press LOAD again until the saved dimensions have been accepted and the destination outline is available.
steps.success_cue: The interface accepts the saved name and dimensions, and a destination bounding box is displayed or the interface is ready to perform the actual load.

steps.action: Close the interface temporarily if necessary and inspect only the bounding box, not any rail result. Confirm that the box is entirely within the intended unobstructed destination and that it has the same dimensions as the source. Reopen the load structure block afterward if the interface was closed.
steps.success_cue: The prepared destination volume has the correct size, does not overlap the source, and the LOAD control is ready for the first actual placement.

steps.action: Trigger the reproduction by clicking LOAD again. This is the first actual placement of rail_art_mc104231 at the destination. Do not click LOAD a further time, place or remove blocks, or otherwise cause additional rail updates before handing control to the observation subsystem.
steps.exact_input: Press LOAD once for the first actual structure placement
steps.success_cue: The structure placement operation has completed at the destination and the game is ready for immediate inspection without a second load having been performed.

stor.handoff_condition: The saved rail structure has just been placed at the unobstructed destination for the first actual time, using 0-degree rotation and no mirror. No second load or manual block update has occurred. Begin observation immediately.
uncertainties: The supplied text does not include the pixels of Step1.png, even though the report states that both the rail geometry and its world directions matter. The exact rail coordinates therefore cannot be encoded from the text alone. Retrieval of Step1.png is an execution-blocking prerequisite; the executor must halt rather than invent a substitute layout if it is unavailable.

The identification of Step1.png as the source-layout image is inferred from its filename and the report's ordering. The attachment should be checked before execution to confirm that it is the pre-load build rather than a post-load result.

The report provides no seed, coordinates, world type, structure dimensions, or rail-placement order. A fresh single-player Superflat world, arbitrary non-overlapping coordinates, and saving all supports with the rails are practical choices rather than asserted requirements.
Single-player is not stated as mandatory. It is selected because no dedicated-server or multiplayer condition appears in the report.

The exact visual wording and arrangement of the Minecraft 1.10 structure-block interface may differ from later interfaces. The operationally important states are SAVE mode, LOAD mode, matching structure name, relative position, stored size, no mirror, and 0-degree rotation.

The command /give @p structure_block 2 is a historically appropriate practical command choice for obtaining two structure blocks in Minecraft 1.10, but the raw report itself does not provide an acquisition command.

Comment 5 documents a separate 180-degree-rotation variant, while Comment 6 confirms that incorrect rails can occur without rotation. This plan follows the original no-rotation first-load procedure and does not substitute the later rotation variant.

source_meta.issue links: Duplicate:inward:MC-152610:woodland mansion shortage the "dark oak leaves " on the fence in 1x1_b3 ("Single bed bedroom") | Relates:inward:MC-271137:Leaves from the Trial Chamber entrance room tree won't decay
source_meta._title: Woodland mansion structure '1x1_b3' has dark oak leaf block with persistent tag set to 'false'

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 1.14.1 in a single-player Creative-mode world with cheats enabled. Use an open, flat area with enough empty space for a small woodland-mansion bedroom template; a new Superflat world is suitable but is not required.
preconditions: Launch the exact Java Edition version Minecraft 1.14.1, which is the first version in the report's affected-version list.
Use a vanilla world without mods or datapacks that replace woodland-mansion structure templates or alter leaf block states.
Create or open a single-player world in Creative mode with cheats enabled. No particular world seed, biome, coordinates, or difficulty is specified by the report.

Move to a flat, unobstructed area with approximately 12 blocks of horizontal clearance and 10 blocks of vertical clearance. Ensure there are no powered redstone components next to the intended command-execution position.
Use default controls where possible. If controls are rebound, use the bindings for Open Chat, Inventory, Sneak, Use Item/Place Block, and Debug Screen.
Do not break or otherwise update the decorative dark oak leaves block after the structure is loaded.

steps.action: Disable reduced debug information so the F3 overlay can display the targeted block's state properties. Press T to open in-game chat, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that the reducedDebugInfo game rule is set to false.

steps.action: Obtain one Block of Redstone for powering the structure block. Press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A Block of Redstone is added to the player's inventory, and command feedback confirms that the item was given.

steps.action: Press E to open the inventory. If the Block of Redstone is not already in the hotbar—the nine slots along the bottom of the inventory—move it into any hotbar slot. Close the inventory with E, then press the corresponding number key from 1 through 9 so the Block of Redstone is the selected item.
steps.success_cue: The player's hand displays a Block of Redstone and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Stand still at the center of the prepared open area on a solid, flat surface. Confirm that the block space occupied by the player's feet is air and that no nearby redstone source can power a block placed there.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary in a clear location, with sufficient empty space around and above the execution point.

steps.action: Place the report's load-mode structure block at the player's current position. Press T, enter the report command exactly as supplied—including the leading slash, capitalization, quotation marks, comma, and structure name—and press Enter. Do not substitute the later /place command because it is unavailable in Minecraft 1.14.1.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback reports that the block was changed. A load-mode structure block is now at the command-execution position; because it was placed at the player's feet, the player may have been moved upward onto its top.

steps.action: Power the newly placed structure block. Keep the Block of Redstone selected, look diagonally downward at one exposed side face of the structure block, hold the Sneak control—Left Shift by default—and right-click the side face once. Sneaking is required so right-click places the Block of Redstone against the structure block instead of opening the structure-block interface.
steps.success_cue: A Block of Redstone is placed directly adjacent to the structure block, providing a new redstone signal to it.

steps.action: Allow the structure load to finish. Do not place or break additional blocks while it loads. Wait until the room blocks have appeared, rendering is complete, and player movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: A small woodland-mansion bedroom template is present, with a birch-plank floor and furnishings that include a bed, fireplace, and decorative indoor plant.

steps.action: Locate the decorative indoor plant within the loaded bedroom. Identify the single dark oak fence used as its stem or stand and the single dark oak leaves block directly on top of that fence. Walk or fly within the room as needed, but do not touch, break, place against, or otherwise update the leaves block.
steps.success_cue: The player has an unobstructed view of the room's only dark oak leaves block, positioned above the dark oak fence.

steps.action: Enable the debug overlay by pressing F3. On keyboards that reserve function keys for hardware controls, press Fn+F3 instead. Confirm that the full debug overlay appears and that reduced debug information is not hiding targeted-block details.
steps.success_cue: The full debug overlay is visible, including a section labeled "Looking at block" when the crosshair is aimed at a block.

steps.action: Move the crosshair precisely onto the decorative leaves block above the dark oak fence. Adjust position or camera angle without interacting with the block until the debug overlay's "Looking at block" section identifies the target as minecraft:dark_oak_leaves and displays its block-state property lines. Stop all input and hand off immediately; do not wait for decay and do not evaluate any property value.
steps.success_cue: The F3 overlay is open, the crosshair is targeting minecraft:dark_oak_leaves, and the targeted block's state-property lines are visible for the observation subsystem.

stor.handoff_condition: The woodland_mansion/1x1_b3 bedroom has been loaded, the F3 debug overlay is enabled, and the crosshair has just targeted the single minecraft:dark_oak_leaves block on top of the dark oak fence. The "Looking at block" state lines are visible, and no blocks have been changed after loading. Begin observation at this point.
uncertainties: The report specifies no world seed, coordinates, world type, biome, difficulty, or server requirement. A single-player Creative world and an open flat test area are practical execution choices rather than report requirements.

The original reproduction command creates a configured structure block but does not itself load the template. A later report comment explicitly says to power the structure block; this plan uses one adjacent Block of Redstone as the simplest deterministic power source.

The report's command is preserved exactly for the recommended Minecraft 1.14.1 version. The later /place template reproduction is not used because /place was introduced after this recommended affected version.

The template's rotation and relative-position fields are left at the defaults produced by the supplied command because the report does not specify alternatives. Consequently, the plant's compass direction relative to the player is not fixed.
Creative mode is not explicitly required by the report, but it avoids survival hazards and provides the permissions and movement needed for deterministic command-based reproduction.

source_meta.issue links: Duplicate:inward:MC-238260:Pillagers not spawning at outpost, guardians not spawning in monuments, mob heads twitching
source_meta._title: Mobs specific to structures aren't spawning in their structures

stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 21w39a in a single-player, newly generated Default world. Use Creative mode with commands available, Generate Structures enabled, Normal difficulty, natural mob spawning enabled for the final observation interval, and render/simulation distances of at least 8 chunks. The selected reproduction variant uses an Ocean Monument and tests post-generation spawning of ordinary Guardians, not the Elder Guardians placed during monument generation.
preconditions: Configure the Minecraft Launcher to start Java Edition snapshot 21w39a, not the fixing snapshot 21w44a or a later release.
Use a separate game directory if possible so the historical snapshot does not open or modify unrelated modern worlds.
Do not use mods, server plugins, or datapacks that alter structures, entity spawning, difficulty, or dimensions.
Create the test world directly in 21w39a; do not upgrade an existing 1.17 or other-version world for this reproduction.
The executor must distinguish an ordinary Guardian from the larger Elder Guardian. Elder Guardians are not the target entity for this test.
Keep the single-player game unpaused during the final natural-spawning interval; opening the Esc pause menu stops the integrated server.

steps.action: Open the Minecraft Launcher, select or create an installation whose version is exactly snapshot 21w39a, and launch it. If snapshots are hidden in the launcher, enable snapshot versions from the Installations screen first.
steps.success_cue: The lower-left or title-screen version text identifies the running game as Minecraft Java Edition 21w39a.

steps.action: From the title screen, select Singleplayer and then select Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Set Game Mode to Creative. Enter any convenient world name; the name does not affect the reproduction.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen displays Game Mode: Creative.

steps.action: Open More World Options. Leave World Type set to Default, ensure Generate Structures is ON, and ensure Allow Cheats is ON. The report supplies no seed for 21w39a, so leave the seed field empty to generate an arbitrary seed.
steps.success_cue: The world is configured as a fresh Default world with structures and commands enabled.

steps.action: Select Create New World and wait for world generation to finish. Do not continue while a loading screen is visible.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the new Overworld, surrounding terrain has rendered, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Press Esc, open Options, then Video Settings. Set Render Distance to at least 8 chunks and Simulation Distance to at least 8 chunks. Select Done as needed to return to the live game.
steps.success_cue: Normal gameplay is visible again, the pause menu is closed, and both distance settings are at least 8 chunks.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat, type the difficulty command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that the difficulty has been set to Normal.

steps.action: Temporarily prevent natural mob spawning while the monument is located and loaded. Press T, type the gamerule command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that the doMobSpawning game rule is now false.

steps.action: Locate the nearest Ocean Monument using the command syntax appropriate to 21w39a. Press T, enter the command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports the coordinates of the nearest Monument rather than displaying an unknown-command or unknown-structure error.

steps.action: Record the horizontal coordinates from the locate result. Treat the first number as X and the last number as Z; if the middle coordinate is displayed as a tilde, it is not needed for the teleport command below.
steps.success_cue: The executor has retained a signed integer X coordinate and a signed integer Z coordinate for the located monument.

steps.action: While in Creative mode, double-tap the default Jump key, Space, to enable Creative flight before teleporting into the air.
steps.success_cue: The player remains suspended when no movement key is held, indicating that Creative flight is active.

steps.action: Press T and teleport above the located monument. Replace <located_X> and <located_Z> with the exact signed coordinates recorded from the locate result; retain Y=100. Include the leading slash and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The teleport succeeds and the player is flying at approximately Y=100 above the located ocean area.

steps.action: Do not issue further setup commands until destination loading finishes. Look downward and allow the ocean and monument chunks to render. The relevant structure is the large prismarine-and-sea-lantern building under the ocean. Wait until the terrain no longer appears incomplete and controls and commands respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The located Ocean Monument area is loaded below the player, the player remains airborne near Y=100, and the game responds normally.

steps.action: Establish a clean baseline for post-generation ordinary Guardian spawning without removing Elder Guardians. Press T, enter the command exactly, and press Enter. A message saying that Guardians were killed or that no matching entity was found is acceptable.
steps.success_cue: No ordinary Guardian that loaded before the observation interval remains; Elder Guardians, whose entity type is different, have not been targeted by the command.

steps.action: Verify that the player has not drifted from the observation position. If necessary, repeat the teleport using the same recorded X and Z values so the player is again flying at Y=100 over the monument.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary in Creative flight at the located monument's X and Z coordinates and approximately Y=100.

steps.action: Re-enable natural mob spawning. Press T, enter the gamerule command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that the doMobSpawning game rule is true.

steps.action: Immediately begin the natural-spawning interval: leave the normal game view open, release all movement controls, remain stationary above the monument for at least five real-time minutes, and do not open the Esc pause menu. Hand control to the observation subsystem at the start of this interval so it can track ordinary Guardian entities separately from Elder Guardians.
steps.success_cue: The world is unpaused, natural spawning is enabled, the monument remains loaded, and the stationary observation interval has started.

stor.handoff_condition: Natural mob spawning has been re-enabled, the freshly generated Ocean Monument is fully loaded, any pre-interval ordinary Guardians have been cleared, and the Creative-mode player is stationary at approximately Y=100 over the monument with the game unpaused. Begin observing entity spawning during the five-minute interval, distinguishing ordinary Guardians from Elder Guardians.
uncertainties: The report does not provide a seed confirmed specifically for 21w39a, so this plan uses /locate monument in a randomly generated fresh world.

The report permits any of Monuments, Witch Huts, or Pillager Outposts. This plan selects one supported deterministic variant—an Ocean Monument—and does not separately exercise the other two structures.

The Y=100 waiting position, temporary doMobSpawning=false setup control, ordinary-Guardian reset command, distance settings, and five-minute interval are operational controls added for deterministic execution; they were not specified by the reporter.
Natural mob spawning is randomized. The five-minute interval provides repeated spawning cycles without requiring excessive repetition, but the report itself specifies no exact waiting duration.

Current launcher screens may label snapshot-selection controls differently from the launcher interface available when 21w39a was released; regardless of UI wording, the launched game version must be exactly 21w39a.

source_meta._title: Camels that spawn within villages can spawn inside blocks

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 22w42a in a new singleplayer world using the integrated server. Use seed -381051283335009767, enable the built-in Update 1.20 experimental data pack during world creation, and enable cheats. Creative mode is selected as a practical convenience because the report does not specify a game mode.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher can install and run historical Java Edition snapshot 22w42a.
Use an unmodified client without gameplay-changing mods or external data packs.
Create a new world; do not reuse an existing world because 22w42a experimental feature flags must be selected during world creation.
Enable the built-in Update 1.20 experimental data pack so that camels are available in 22w42a.
Enable cheats so the report's teleport command can be executed in in-game chat.
Do not preload or manually visit the target coordinates before executing the specified teleport; the target village and its camel should be allowed to load through the reproduction sequence.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select a Java Edition installation that uses the historical snapshot 22w42a, then launch that installation.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft reaches the main menu and the displayed version text identifies the running client as 22w42a.

steps.action: From the main menu, select Singleplayer, then select Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Set Game Mode to Creative. Ensure Allow Cheats is set to ON; if selecting Creative turns cheats on automatically, leave them enabled.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows Creative mode and Allow Cheats: ON.

steps.action: Open More World Options and enter the report's seed into the Seed for the World Generator field. Preserve the leading minus sign and all digits exactly.
steps.success_cue: The seed field contains exactly -381051283335009767.

steps.action: From the world-creation options, open Data Packs. In the Available list, locate the built-in pack labeled Update 1.20, internally associated with update_1_20, and use its arrow control to move it to the Selected list.
steps.success_cue: The Update 1.20 built-in data pack appears in the Selected or enabled data-pack list.

steps.action: Select Done to return from the Data Packs screen. If an experimental-features warning or confirmation dialog appears, confirm that the world should use the selected experimental settings.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is restored with the Update 1.20 experimental features retained.

steps.action: Select Create New World and accept any final experimental-world warning. Do not change the seed or data-pack selection before creating the world.
steps.success_cue: The new world opens and the player appears at the initial Overworld spawn location.

steps.action: Wait only until the initial spawn terrain has rendered and the player responds normally to input. Do not explore toward the target village.
steps.success_cue: Nearby spawn chunks are visible and the game responds normally to movement or camera input.

steps.action: Press T, or the currently bound Open Chat control, to open in-game chat.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is visible and ready to receive a command.

steps.action: Enter the report's command exactly as written, including the leading slash, coordinates, yaw, and pitch, then press Enter once. Executing this command is the trigger because it moves the player into the target village area and causes the destination chunks to load or generate.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted and the player is teleported to approximately X=-446.99, Y=72.00, Z=2502.34 in the Overworld with yaw -23.39 and pitch 6.11.

steps.action: Keep the supplied position and viewing direction unchanged. Wait only until the destination terrain and nearby desert-village blocks have rendered and the client responds normally; do not walk, turn away, break or place blocks, interact with the camel, or allow additional unnecessary time to pass.
steps.success_cue: The desert-village area around the teleport destination is rendered, the game is responsive, and the player remains at the supplied coordinates and orientation.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just teleported to X=-446.99, Y=72.00, Z=2502.34 in the Overworld, the nearby desert-village terrain has finished rendering, and the supplied position and viewing direction have been preserved. Immediately hand control to the observation subsystem to inspect the village camel and the blocks directly around it.
uncertainties: The deterministic seed and coordinates in the description are explicitly labeled as an example for version 1.19.3, while the first listed affected version and therefore the required recommended version is 22w42a. The report does not explicitly confirm that this exact location produces the same arrangement in 22w42a. If it does not, the same procedure can be rerun in the explicitly documented example version 1.19.3, with the Update 1.20 experimental features still enabled.

The report does not specify a game mode or multiplayer requirement. Singleplayer Creative mode with cheats enabled is used as the simplest execution path and is not asserted as a condition of the bug.
Depending on the exact 22w42a interface text, the built-in experimental pack may be displayed as Update 1.20 rather than its internal-style identifier update_1_20.
Comment 9 says 22w14a, but the formal Affects versions field lists 23w14a. The affected_versions output preserves the formal field exactly as required.

The report does not identify a particular village component for the original seed beyond the blocks surrounding the camel; the separate comment mentioning a fountain refers to a different seed and coordinates and was therefore not substituted into this plan.

source_meta._title: Dimension padding doesn't affect the start piece

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 24w20a; new singleplayer Overworld; Creative mode; commands enabled; the unmodified attached data pack dimension_padding_bug_report.zip enabled before world creation. The data pack replaces/modifies the plains-village structure definition so that dimension_padding is 158.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher is available and configured to show snapshot installations.
Minecraft: Java Edition 24w20a is installed or can be selected in the launcher.
The exact Mojira attachment dimension_padding_bug_report.zip has been downloaded and remains available as a ZIP file; do not reconstruct, rename internally, or replace it with a different data pack.
Use a newly created world so that the data pack's world-generation changes are active before any candidate village chunks generate.
No world seed or village coordinates were supplied, so the procedure may require searching several plains villages.
Do not use fix version 24w44a for this reproduction.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select a Java Edition installation using version 24w20a, then start the game with that installation.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu opens and identifies the running version as 24w20a.

steps.action: From the main menu, select Singleplayer, then select Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: On the world configuration screen, set Game Mode to Creative and make sure Allow Commands is On. Leave the world type as the normal/default Overworld generator; the report does not supply a seed, so the seed field may remain empty.
steps.success_cue: Creative mode is selected, commands are allowed, and the world has not yet been created.

steps.action: Open the More tab, select Data Packs, and add dimension_padding_bug_report.zip by dragging the ZIP into the Minecraft window or by selecting Open Pack Folder and copying the ZIP into the opened folder. Accept the confirmation prompt if Minecraft asks whether to add the pack. Data packs can be enabled during creation of a singleplayer world. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3AInstalling_a_data_pack?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: An entry corresponding to dimension_padding_bug_report.zip appears in the Available data packs list or is already shown in the Selected list.

steps.action: If the data pack is in the Available list, select the arrow on its icon to move it to the Selected/enabled side. Do not enable unrelated third-party data packs. Select Done to return to world configuration.
steps.success_cue: dimension_padding_bug_report.zip is on the Selected side before leaving the Data Packs screen.

steps.action: Select Create New World. If an experimental-settings or data-pack warning appears, acknowledge it and continue because this is a disposable reproduction world created specifically with the supplied world-generation pack.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft begins creating the new world with the supplied data pack enabled.

steps.action: Wait until the player appears in the Overworld, surrounding terrain has rendered, and movement responds normally. Do not travel extensively before verifying the data pack.
steps.success_cue: The player is controllable in a newly generated Overworld.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat, enter the data-pack listing command including the leading slash, and press Enter. This is a verification step; no /reload is needed because the pack was enabled before world creation. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3AInstalling_a_data_pack?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The enabled-pack output includes an entry corresponding to file/dimension_padding_bug_report.zip. If it does not, stop and recreate the world after correctly enabling the attachment.

steps.action: Press T, enter the locate command including the leading slash, and press Enter. The command targets the plains-village configured structure specifically, rather than the tag containing all village types. The Java Edition locate syntax uses the structure subcommand and accepts a configured structure identifier. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_1.18.2_Pre-release_1?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: Chat reports coordinates for the nearest minecraft:village_plains structure.

steps.action: Record the X and Z coordinates returned by the locate command. In a coordinate triplet, use the first number as X and the third number as Z; the search result's displayed Y value is not used for the safe arrival command.
steps.success_cue: The located plains village's X and Z values are available for substitution into the next command.

steps.action: Press T and enter the teleport command below, replacing <X_FROM_LOCATE> and <Z_FROM_LOCATE> with the exact integers reported in step 9. Keep Y set to 200 so the player arrives above ordinary terrain rather than inside blocks. Press Enter. Absolute X, Y, and Z coordinates are valid with /tp. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3ACommand_blocks_and_functions?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The player teleports to Y=200 above the located plains-village area.

steps.action: Do not issue another command immediately. Wait until the terrain below has rendered, nearby chunks stop visibly appearing, and movement responds normally. Loading these previously ungenerated chunks is the generation trigger for this candidate village.
steps.success_cue: The candidate village area and its surrounding terrain are fully rendered and responsive.

steps.action: If not already flying, double-tap Space to enable Creative flight. Look downward, hold the Sneak/descend control (default Left Shift) to reduce altitude, and use movement controls such as W to approach the located structure without breaking or placing blocks.
steps.exact_input: Double-tap Space; hold Left Shift to descend
steps.success_cue: The player is close enough to inspect the candidate plains village while remaining in Creative mode.

steps.action: Identify the village's start piece by locating its town-center or meeting-point piece near the locate coordinates, rather than selecting an outlying house, farm, or path. Plains-village town-center templates can use gathering features such as a fountain/well, market stalls, a tree plaza, and bells. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Village/Structure?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The player has identified the candidate village's central meeting-point/start-piece area.

steps.action: Press F3 to open the debug overlay. Stand beside the town-center piece and aim the crosshair at a floor, base, or foundation block belonging to that central piece. Read the Y coordinate for the targeted block. Do not break blocks. Accept the candidate only when that town-center block has Y=93 or lower, which is below Y94; a value of Y=90 or lower is preferable to avoid ambiguity at the boundary.
steps.success_cue: Either the town-center/start-piece area has been confirmed below Y94, or the candidate has been classified as too high and must be rejected.

steps.action: If the town-center block checked in step 15 is below Y94, leave the candidate village loaded and proceed directly to handoff. Do not enter a command, place blocks, break blocks, or travel away before handoff.
steps.success_cue: An enabled-pack plains-village candidate whose town-center/start-piece area is below Y94 remains fully loaded for observation.

steps.action: Only if the candidate's town center is at Y94 or higher, press T and teleport 5000 blocks along the positive X axis while returning to Y=200. Press Enter, wait for movement to respond normally, and then return to step 9 to locate the nearest plains village from the new search area. Repeat steps 9 through 17 until a candidate below Y94 is found.
steps.success_cue: The player is approximately 5000 blocks away from the rejected candidate and is ready to perform a new plains-village locate search.

stor.handoff_condition: The final candidate's previously ungenerated chunks have just been loaded after the teleport in step 11, the supplied dimension-padding data pack is confirmed enabled, and the identified plains-village town-center/start-piece area is below Y94. The player remains beside or above that center area without modifying it; begin observation of the generated structure layout.
uncertainties: The raw report does not include the contents of dimension_padding_bug_report.zip. This plan therefore requires the exact Mojira attachment and does not attempt to recreate its JSON files.
No deterministic world seed or coordinates were supplied. Finding a plains village below Y94 may require multiple locate-and-teleport iterations, as the report itself notes.

The report says the village must 'start below y94' but does not define an in-game measurement procedure. Step 15 uses a block belonging to the town-center/start-piece base or floor as the practical height check and recommends selecting a candidate clearly below the threshold.
The report lists 24w20a first, so it is the required recommended reproduction version even though later affected versions are also listed.

External verification was limited to allowed Minecraft Wiki material for world-creation data-pack installation, historical locate syntax, teleport syntax, and identification of plains-village town-center templates.
